answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because knoll only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any pulse approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
